correctness.rationale: For each factor, unique maximal-index symbol fixes a rank-centered occurrence set E_{r,j}; its earliest endpoint parametrizes the states and the entire transition map. Distinct states have distinct longest continuation lengths. The finite checker independently reproduces all factors/endsets for ranks 1–7 and standard suffix automata for ranks 1–11. Infinity follows from a complete all-rank occurrence proof, not finite extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The assessed claim is the complete labelled right-context graph, the joint factor/suffix interpretation, and the per-letter transition spectrum for every rank. Generic automata results and the 2013 literal factor-membership criterion do not give this labelled graph. The total-edge arithmetic sequence is already in OEIS A132925 without a Zimin-automaton interpretation. An overlapping general paper from 2011 was not available in full; priority is qualified, not asserted to be exhaustively established.
residual_risks: The full text of Fici 2011 was inaccessible; conclusions about its specific Zimin coverage are limited to the abstract and related 2009 presentation.
An unindexed Zimin-automaton treatment or derivation from episturmian automata might predate this description.
The total arc-count formula itself is in OEIS A132925; only the graph structure and its Zimin interpretation are assessed as new.

value.rationale: This is a complete labelled minimal-DFA classification for an exponentially long classical recursive word, including all canonical right-context states and a letter-resolved transition inventory. Its arithmetic description permits substring recognition without materializing the graph. It adds structural information beyond an existing scalar sequence, routine state lower bounds or known generic membership algorithms.
